Since the issue arises in the appeals are one and the same, the same are disposed of by way of this common order.

2. The Insurance Company has come forward with these appeals, against the judgment and decree dated 26.08.2013 and made in MCOP. Nos.36 and 37 of 2016, dated 14.11.2018 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, (II Additional District & Sessions Judge) Chidambaram.
3.

sentences.text: It is the case of the appellant that the first respondent in in CMA.No.1037 of 2020 is father and the first respondent in CMA.No.1038 of 2020 is his daughter.

On 30.08.2013 at 10.00 p.m. the father was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg. no.TN 68 E 0936 and the daughter was travelling as pillion rider, at that time, a lorry was coming https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis in the opposite direction

, the second respondent's Tata sumo bearing Reg. No.TN 51 R 4187 driven by its driver, the third respondent, was coming behind the lorry, rash and negligently, overtaking the lorry and dashed against the two wheeler, which was driven by the first respondent Nagaraj, for which, the father and daughter sustained grievous injuries and admitted in a hospital for treatment.

Thereafter,
both the injured persons have filed separate claim petition before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal claiming compensation.
The Tribunal considering the pleadings, oral and documentary evidence, passed common award in favour of the first respondent.
Aggrieved over the same, both the appeals have filed by the insurance company.
4.The learned counsel appearing for the appellant Insurance company submitted that the award passed by the Tribunal is highly excessive, exorbitant and unsustainable.

The learned counsel further submitted that the police has not filed charge sheet against the driver of the Tata sumo and the accident was caused due to reckless driving of unknown swift Maruti car by marking Ex.C1 and the investigation report has proved that the TATA Sumo has not involved in the accident.
Before the Tribunal, the claimants themselves stated that an unknown car has caused the accident.
Further, the rider of the two wheeler has no driving license.
Without considering the entire fact, the Tribunal has awarded https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis huge compensation to the claimants, which warrants interference of this Court.

5. Per contra, the learned counsel appearing for the first respondent in both the appeals contended that the Tribunal, after analyzing the materials available on record, has rightly awarded the quantum of compensation and hence, no interference in required and therefore, the appeals have to be dismissed.

sentences.text:
There is no representation on behalf of the respondents 3 & 4.
7.
The facts of the case are not in dispute.

The main ground on which the appellant assails the award passed by the Tribunal is that the FIR which is the earliest document which was given by the claimants relating to the accident reveals that the claimants have made a categorical admission that an unknown Swift Maruti Car had dashed against the vehicle in which the claimants were riding.

However, the vehicle insured with the appellant is a TATA Sumo Car and the type of car is totally not https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis matching which clearly shows that the car insured with the appellant has been roped only for the purpose of getting compensation at the hands of the appellant.
In this regard, the appellant plays reliance on Ex.P1 and also Ex.R1 and therefore, submits that the claim made as against appellant cannot be maintained.
It is to be pointed out that though Ex.P1/FIR is the earliest document.
However, it has been held by the courts in catena of decisions that the FIR is not an encyclopedia and all the information need not be given in the FIR so as to make the FIR, a complete one.

The FIR which is given at the earliest point of time is only for the purpose of registering the crime, at which point, as in this case, the claimants who have been hit by the offending vehicle would not have been aware of the type of vehicle which had hit them not would they have been able to identify the registration number of the vehicle which has hit them.
Even before the Doctor, the claimants have spoken that an unknown vehicle had hit them.
Merely because Ex.R1 final report has been filed by the law enforcing agency referring the crime as a mistake of fact

,
cannot be the basis to negative the case of the claimants that the vehicle insured with the appellant was not involved in the accident.
Exs. R2
and 3 which have been filed by the appellant insurer relating to their enquiry
cannot be made the basis to hold that the complaint given by the claimants is false or is a fabricated one.

Unless the materials which https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis clearly run counter to the case of the claimants are placed by the respondents, the mere fact that there is a difference between the complaint and the subsequent claim made against the offending vehicle cannot be the basis to reject the case of the claimants.
8. In the case on hand, the accident had not been disputed.
But only the involvement of the of the vehicle insured with the appellant is in dispute.

In the absence of any materials by the appellant to disprove that the vehicle insured with the appellant was not involved in the accident, definitely weightage has to be given to the position of PW1 and PW2 who are injured victims in the said accident.
Therefore, rightly appreciating all the aforesaid materials and considering the issue in proper prospective.
The discrepancy between the FIR and the deposition has been appreciated by the Tribunal to give a finding that the vehicle insured with the appellant was involved in the accident.
Therefore, the said finding is not required any interference by this Court.
9. Further, the Tribunal has awarded compensation in respect of loss of income and applied multiplier method which is not applicable in the present case and hence the same is modified.
The accident has happened in the year 2013 and the Doctor has assessed the disability for https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis the victims at 56% and 28% respectively.
Therefore, for loss of income, this Court fixes the compensation at Rs. 3000/- per percentage to the claimants.
